onboarding.desc: The agent is a small program that runs in your home network and delivers wake commands to your devices.

hero.title: Wake your home network, from anywhere.
hero.subtitle: A secret crosses the cloud, and the machine at home lights up.
hero.facts: no open ports · no exposed LAN · the server only sees ciphertext
hero.diagramAlt: Topology: the browser sends an RSA-encrypted MAC over TLS to the WakeWake server on a 2 GB VPS; the agent at home holds an outbound SSE connection and broadcasts a UDP magic packet to wake the device
hero.noteBrowser: Plaintext MAC never leaves your browser
hero.noteAgent: Dials out only — no inbound ports

hop1.title: Encrypted in your browser
hop1.body: Your browser encrypts the MAC with the agent's public key. From receipt to database, the server only ever sees ciphertext.

hop2.title: The agent dials out, and only out
hop2.body: The agent holds an outbound SSE connection, and commands ride it home. No inbound port points at your house — zero router configuration.

hop3.title: A magic packet lights it up
hop3.body: The agent decrypts the MAC and broadcasts a magic packet on your LAN. It never scans, forwards, or proxies anything.

trust.title: The hard questions, asked first
trust.q1: What if the whole database is stolen?
trust.a1: Nothing useful. MACs are encrypted in the browser; the database holds only RSA-OAEP ciphertext. The private key lives on the agent's disk — and nowhere else.
trust.q2: Do I need open ports or a public IP at home?
trust.a2: Neither. The agent only dials out, so there is no inbound hole pointing at your home. Your router stays untouched.
trust.q3: If the server is fully compromised, what's the worst case?
trust.a3: At worst, replaying old ciphertexts to boot devices you already registered. It cannot read MACs, cannot forge new devices, and cannot reach into your LAN.
trust.q4: What about the rest of my LAN?
trust.a4: Untouched. The agent sends broadcast magic packets and nothing else — no scanning, no forwarding, no proxying.

deploy.title: Three commands, on your own VPS
deploy.body: One multi-arch image, fronted by Caddy. Migrations and the bootstrap admin run automatically at startup — there is no migration step to forget.
deploy.terminalLabel: compose · a 2 GB VPS is enough
